upright.meaning: The Fool steps toward the cliff's edge in joyous trust, and the universe catches every sincere leap of faith.

reversed.meaning: The same leap taken blindly becomes a stumble, so look before the heart hurls itself forward.

upright.meaning: Every tool lies on the table before him, because everything needed to begin the great work is already in your hands.

reversed.meaning: Power misdirected curdles into trickery, or talent left sleeping gathers dust instead of gold.

upright.meaning: Behind her veil the moonlit waters hold answers that only silence and patience can draw to the surface.

reversed.meaning: When the inner voice is drowned out by chatter, you grope in a darkness of your own making.

upright.meaning: She reclines in a field of ripening wheat, and everything she touches grows lush, generous, and alive.

reversed.meaning: Care curdles into control, or the garden of your making withers from neglect.

upright.meaning: His stone throne is built on order, and from that order rises the safety in which empires and families can thrive.

reversed.meaning: Command hardens into tyranny when the scepter forgets that it serves the realm, not the reverse.

upright.meaning: Between the pillars of established wisdom he raises a hand in blessing, for some truths are carried, not invented.

reversed.meaning: When the ritual matters more than the meaning, the wise break the rule to save the faith.

upright.meaning: Two souls stand beneath the blessing angel, and the heart's true choice aligns desire with conscience.

reversed.meaning: A bond strained by divided loyalties, or a choice made against the grain of your own values.

upright.meaning: He drives the sphinxes of opposing forces with a steady gaze, and disciplined will carries him to triumph.

reversed.meaning: The reins slip when the destination is unclear, and force without direction merely spins in place.

upright.meaning: She closes the lion's mouth with a soft hand, proving that true strength tames rather than crushes.

reversed.meaning: When gentleness fails, the inner beast either cowers in fear or lashes out unchecked.

upright.meaning: His lantern lights only the next step, because wisdom is found by walking inward, alone, in the dark.

reversed.meaning: Solitude sours into exile when the lamp is shuttered and no one is let in at all.

upright.meaning: The great wheel turns above sphinx and serpent alike, lifting the low and lowering the high in its endless round.

reversed.meaning: Clinging to the rim while the wheel spins only bruises you; the turn comes whether you bless it or not.

upright.meaning: Her scales weigh every deed without flinching, and what is sown in truth is reaped in kind.

reversed.meaning: The scales tip when judgment is bought, bent, or dodged, and the debt of truth always comes due.

upright.meaning: He hangs willingly, upside down, and in that stillness the world rearranges itself into a clearer pattern.

reversed.meaning: A pause stretched past its purpose becomes mere delay, or sacrifice offered where none was asked.

upright.meaning: The skeletal knight rides on, and what falls before him clears the ground where a new life is already stirring.

reversed.meaning: Refusing to bury what is already dead only chains you to a corpse instead of freeing the living.

upright.meaning: She pours water between the cups in an unbroken stream, blending opposites into a golden, healing middle way.

reversed.meaning: Too much of anything, even a good thing, spills the vessel and sours the mixture.

upright.meaning: The chained figures could slip their loose collars at any time, yet stay: such is the grip of appetite mistaken for need.

reversed.meaning: The collar is seen for what it is at last, and the first honest step out of the old compulsion begins.

upright.meaning: Lightning strikes the crown of the false tower, and though the fall is terrifying, only lies are destroyed.

reversed.meaning: The crack spreads quietly within, or a collapse long feared finally forces the rebuilding to begin.

upright.meaning: She pours starlight into pool and earth alike, and after the storm the soul breathes easy in naked, quiet hope.

reversed.meaning: The stars are still there, only clouded; hope deferred is not hope destroyed, but it needs tending.

upright.meaning: Between the twin towers the moon drips its pale light, and half-seen shapes stir the fears that daylight keeps at bay.

reversed.meaning: The fog thins and the imagined monsters shrink back into shadow as truth steps into the moonlight.

upright.meaning: The child rides out under the blazing sun, and everything ripens in the warmth of simple, unashamed happiness.

reversed.meaning: A brief eclipse dims the light: happiness delayed or taken for granted, but never truly gone.

upright.meaning: The trumpet sounds and the dead rise from their coffins, answering at last the higher calling they were born for.

reversed.meaning: The call sounds but you cover your ears, or the past is judged again instead of forgiven.

upright.meaning: She dances within the laurel wreath as the four beasts watch, and the long journey closes in perfect, joyful completion.

reversed.meaning: The wreath is woven but one strand hangs loose; finish the final task and the circle will close.

upright.meaning: A hand offers a blazing wand from the clouds: pure fire to ignite any new enterprise.

reversed.meaning: The spark sputters when scattered in too many directions or struck before its time.

upright.meaning: He holds the world in one hand and a wand in the other, choosing which horizon his ambition will conquer.

reversed.meaning: Grand plans wither when choice is endlessly postponed or made without counsel.

upright.meaning: His ships return laden across the water: ventures launched with vision come home bearing fruit.

reversed.meaning: The ships are becalmed; progress stalls and foresight goes unrewarded for a season.

upright.meaning: Garlands crown the four wands as dancers celebrate a foundation well and truly laid.

reversed.meaning: The celebration is postponed, or the milestone reveals the next road already calling.

upright.meaning: Five youths clash their staves in mock battle: friction that tests strength and sharpens skill.

reversed.meaning: The skirmish burns itself out, though embers of tension may still smolder within.

upright.meaning: Crowned with laurel he rides through the cheering crowd: effort recognized and victory made public.

reversed.meaning: The laurel is delayed, or triumph curdles into vanity when applause becomes the goal.

upright.meaning: From the high ground he beats back six attackers: one person's conviction holding against the many.

reversed.meaning: The high ground is lost, or the fight costs more than the hill was ever worth.

upright.meaning: Eight wands fly straight as arrows through clear air: things move fast now, and messages fly true.

reversed.meaning: The arrows scatter in a crosswind; haste tangles what patience would have ordered.

upright.meaning: Wounded but upright, he guards the line of wands behind him: one more effort will see it through.

reversed.meaning: The guard is worn past bearing, or old battles are refought long after the war is won.

upright.meaning: He staggers under ten heavy wands toward a distant town: the price of carrying everything alone.

reversed.meaning: The bundle is set down at last, or dropped in collapse, and the load is finally shared.

upright.meaning: A bright-eyed youth lifts his wand toward unmapped horizons: the fearless messenger of new adventures.

reversed.meaning: Enthusiasm outruns preparation, and the eager messenger arrives with the wrong news.

upright.meaning: He charges into the fray with plume flying: the bold champion who acts first and apologizes later.

reversed.meaning: The charge becomes a rout when courage forgets counsel and fire forgets its hearth.

upright.meaning: She rules from a throne of lions and sunflowers: warm, commanding, and impossible to ignore.

reversed.meaning: Her fire turns inward to smolder as envy, or outward to scorch all who approach.

upright.meaning: He surveys his realm with a wand of living wood: the entrepreneur-king who turns vision into dominion.

reversed.meaning: Command hardens into bluster, and grand visions burn out for lack of steady tending.

upright.meaning: A hand offers an overflowing cup beneath the dove of spirit: the heart opens to love, art, or grace.

reversed.meaning: The cup is stoppered; feelings dammed up turn stagnant instead of flowing.

upright.meaning: Two cups are exchanged beneath the winged lion: a bond of equals, sealed in trust and tenderness.

reversed.meaning: The exchange falters when giving and taking fall out of rhythm, or trust is bent.

upright.meaning: Three maidens dance with raised cups: joy multiplied by friendship and shared in good company.

reversed.meaning: The dance grows rowdy, or whispered words sour the sweetness of the gathering.

upright.meaning: He sits beneath the tree, arms crossed, blind to the fourth cup offered by spirit: a pause to reconsider what truly satisfies.

reversed.meaning: The offered cup is noticed at last, and stagnant discontent gives way to fresh engagement.

upright.meaning: Cloaked in black he mourns the three spilled cups, not yet seeing the two that stand unbroken behind him.

reversed.meaning: Mourning lifts; the spilled wine is forgiven and the cups still standing are lifted again.

upright.meaning: Children exchange cups of flowers in a sunlit courtyard: the sweetness of memory and simple kindness.

reversed.meaning: The past becomes a cage instead of a garden when memory is clung to instead of cherished.

upright.meaning: Seven cups float in a glittering cloud of visions: dreams dazzle, but not every shining cup holds wine.

reversed.meaning: The mist clears and one true cup is chosen; illusion yields to committed choice.

upright.meaning: He abandons the stacked cups beneath an eclipsed moon, turning toward higher ground the heart cannot name.

reversed.meaning: The road is seen but not taken, and the soul sits among cups it has outgrown.

upright.meaning: The satisfied merchant sits before his nine arranged cups: the wish granted and savored in full.

reversed.meaning: The wish granted proves empty, or pleasure pursued for its own sake leaves the heart hungry.

upright.meaning: Beneath the rainbow of ten cups a family dances in the cottage garden: love made complete and enduring.

reversed.meaning: The rainbow fades when home's harmony is strained, though the cups themselves remain unbroken.

upright.meaning: A dreamy youth gazes at the fish rising from his cup: tender new feelings surfacing from the deep.

reversed.meaning: Feelings spill sideways into sulks or daydreams when the young heart cannot name them.

upright.meaning: He rides gently forward, cup extended: the romantic who follows his heart with grace and courtesy.

reversed.meaning: The suitor's vows dissolve like mist, or charm masks a heart that will not commit.

upright.meaning: She contemplates her ornate cup in stillness: the empath whose quiet waters run fathomlessly deep.

reversed.meaning: Her waters flood their banks: feeling everything, she drowns in others' tides or her own.

upright.meaning: He sits steady upon his throne amid tossing waves: mastery of feeling expressed as calm, wise counsel.

reversed.meaning: The calm sea hides a riptide: feelings weaponized, or composure cracking under hidden strain.

upright.meaning: A hand grips a sword crowned with laurel and olive: truth cutting through confusion in one decisive stroke.

reversed.meaning: The blade is double-edged when turned carelessly: clarity muddied, or truth wielded as a weapon.

upright.meaning: Blindfolded she balances two crossed swords beneath the moon: a fragile peace while a hard choice waits.

reversed.meaning: The blindfold slips, or is torn off, and the long-avoided decision can no longer wait.

upright.meaning: Three swords pierce the floating heart beneath gray rain: sorrow that must be felt to be healed.

reversed.meaning: The swords are drawn out one by one; the wound closes and the heart learns to beat freely again.

upright.meaning: The knight lies in effigy above his tomb while one sword rests below: sacred rest before the next battle.

reversed.meaning: Rest refused becomes exhaustion; the tomb is no place to sleep when the battle still calls.

upright.meaning: He gathers the fallen swords with a smirk while the defeated walk away: winning at too high a cost.

reversed.meaning: The swords are laid down and peace is attempted, though old wounds may still ache beneath.

upright.meaning: The ferryman poles toward the far shore where the water smooths: sorrowful passage toward quieter days.

reversed.meaning: The boat circles in rough water; the far shore is refused or the passage is delayed.

upright.meaning: He slips away with five swords while two stand planted: cunning that wins the prize, or steals it.

reversed.meaning: The theft is discovered or confessed; what was taken by stealth must now be reckoned with.

upright.meaning: Bound and blindfolded among eight swords, she could walk free: the cage is built mostly of her own thoughts.

reversed.meaning: The bindings loosen as the mind clears; the first step out of the prison is finally taken.

upright.meaning: She sits upright in bed, head in hands, beneath nine hanging swords: the terrors that daylight dissolves.

reversed.meaning: The long night ends; fears faced in daylight shrink to their proper, manageable size.

upright.meaning: Face down beneath ten swords at dawn's red edge: the worst has happened, and with it the end of suffering.

reversed.meaning: The swords are being drawn from the back one by one; healing begins, though scars remain tender.

upright.meaning: A keen youth raises his sword to a shifting sky: the sharp mind ever watchful for the next new idea.

reversed.meaning: The keen edge turns to cutting remarks, or cleverness chases rumors instead of truth.

upright.meaning: He charges headlong into the storm, sword raised: intellect at full gallop, brilliant and unstoppable.

reversed.meaning: The charge outruns judgment; brilliance becomes bluster and words become weapons.

upright.meaning: She raises her sword upright on a throne of air: sorrow has sharpened her into truth's clearest witness.

reversed.meaning: Clarity curdles into cruelty when the heart's frost silences its warmth entirely.

upright.meaning: Enthroned among butterflies of transformation, he rules by reason: the just strategist none can deceive.

reversed.meaning: Reason becomes rationalization, and the sharp mind schemes for itself instead of serving justice.

upright.meaning: A hand offers a golden coin above a flowering garden: the seed of material blessing, ready to be planted.

reversed.meaning: The coin slips through careless fingers, or the seed is planted in barren, unready ground.

upright.meaning: He dances with two coins in an endless loop amid the waves: keeping everything in the air with grace.

reversed.meaning: Too many coins in the air at once; the dance falters and something precious drops.

upright.meaning: The artisan's work rises in the cathedral while patrons admire: skill honored through collaboration.

reversed.meaning: Shoddy craft or clashing egos; the cathedral suffers when the builders will not listen.

upright.meaning: Crowned and enthroned, he clutches his coins: the safety of what is held, and the fear of letting go.

reversed.meaning: The grip loosens into generosity, or the coins are flung away in a panic of release.

upright.meaning: Two beggars limp past the lit church window in the snow: hard times endured outside the warmth.

reversed.meaning: The church door opens at last; help is found, or the worst of the winter passes.

upright.meaning: The merchant weighs coins into open hands: wealth flowing where it is needed, given with grace.

reversed.meaning: Giving comes with hooks, or the scales of debt tip beyond what can be repaid.

upright.meaning: He leans on his hoe, studying the growing vines: honest work appraised with a farmer's patient eye.

reversed.meaning: The harvest is judged too soon, or labor poured into soil that was never going to bear.

upright.meaning: The craftsman hammers coin after coin at his bench: mastery built one careful repetition at a time.

reversed.meaning: The bench becomes a treadmill: endless detail with no craft, or skill left unlearned.

upright.meaning: She stands in her walled garden with falcon on wrist: independence cultivated into graceful abundance.

reversed.meaning: The garden walls become a gilded cage, or abundance is chased until it owns the chaser.

upright.meaning: Three generations gather beneath the arch of ten coins: prosperity rooted deep enough to outlast its makers.

reversed.meaning: The arch cracks when kin quarrel over the coins, or riches prove as temporary as seasons.

upright.meaning: The youth studies his single coin with total absorption: the patient student of the material world.

reversed.meaning: The coin is gazed at but never spent; study without application bears no harvest.

upright.meaning: He sits motionless upon his heavy horse, coin in hand: the plodding guardian who never abandons his post.

reversed.meaning: Steadfastness hardens into stubborn ruts, or duty becomes drudgery without end.

upright.meaning: She cradles her coin amid rabbits and roses: the earth-mother who makes prosperity feel like home.

reversed.meaning: The garden or the household suffers while she tends the other; care itself needs caring for.

upright.meaning: Enthroned among vines and bulls, he rests a foot on abundance itself: wealth built to shelter generations.

reversed.meaning: The throne is gilded but hollow when profit is worshipped and the kingdom's soul is sold.
